Fit the contamination-mixture model from design matrices

Source: R/mixture_core.R
mixture_fit_matrix.Rd

Low-level interface that takes design matrices directly, mirroring the original research functions fit_mixture(), fit_logit_mixture() and fit_pois_mixture(). Most users should call mixture_fit(), which builds the design matrices from a formula and calls this function.

Usage

mixture_fit_matrix(
  Xp,
  yp,
  Xnp,
  ynp,
  family = "gaussian",
  model = c("Mjoint", "M0", "M1"),
  leverage = NULL,
  n_iter = 3000,
  burnin = 1500,
  thin = 1,
  seed = NULL,
  prior = mixture_prior(),
  control = mixture_control(),
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

Xp, Xnp

Numeric design matrices (including an intercept column, if wanted) for the probability (P) and non-probability (NP) samples. Both must have the same columns.

yp, ynp

Outcome vectors for the P and NP samples.

family

One of "gaussian", "binomial" (logistic regression for a 0/1, logical or two-level factor response) or "poisson". A family object such as binomial() is also accepted (only its name is used; the links are fixed to identity, logit and log respectively).

model

Contamination model: "Mjoint" (default), "M0" or "M1"; see the Model section.

leverage

Integer column indices (or column names) of Xp/Xnp that enter the covariate density of model "Mjoint"; typically the continuous predictors. Equivalent to cont_idx in the original code. Ignored for models "M0" and "M1".

n_iter

Total number of MCMC iterations, including burn-in.

burnin

Number of initial iterations discarded.

thin

Keep every thin-th post-burn-in draw.

seed

Optional random seed. When supplied the fit is reproducible and the global random-number stream is restored afterwards; when NULL the current stream is used.

prior

Prior hyperparameters, see mixture_prior().

control

Algorithm settings, see mixture_control().

verbose

If TRUE, report progress every 10% of iterations.

Value

An object of class bsm_fit; see mixture_fit().

Examples

set.seed(1)
Xp <- cbind(1, rnorm(100)); yp <- drop(Xp %*% c(2, 5)) + rnorm(100)
Xnp <- cbind(1, rnorm(100)); ynp <- drop(Xnp %*% c(2, 5)) + rnorm(100)
ynp[1:25] <- rnorm(25, -20)          # 25% contaminated outcomes
fit <- mixture_fit_matrix(Xp, yp, Xnp, ynp, leverage = 2,
                          n_iter = 600, burnin = 200, seed = 1)
coef(fit)
#>       x1       x2 
#> 1.967023 5.059751
